transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to flag a critical issue before any approval is given. Yesterday I received a soil laboratory report for the courtyard, and it found lead at 185 parts per million in the existing soil. That's above our district's 100-ppm threshold. District procedure requires us to remove the top 8 inches of soil and replace it with certified clean soil before students can use the garden. This report is still sitting in my facilities folder awaiting weekly review and has not yet been added to the project proposal. This needs to be factored into the plan, the timeline, and the budget before we finalize anything.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I have important information that affects this proposal significantly. The science department's executed garden-learning grant, which I received the terms for just this week, requires the project to include exactly 10 native plant species — not the six currently in the proposal. It also requires exactly 6 science lessons in the garden by November 1, 2026 — not the three currently planned. Additionally, the grant requires supervised maintenance to be scheduled on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m. The proposal was drafted before the grant award was finalized, so it doesn't yet reflect these binding requirements. All of these grant terms need to be incorporated into the plan before we finalize approval.

transcript.text: Thank you, Mr. Ellis. That's very important — the grant terms are binding, and the proposal as currently written doesn't comply with them. So we now have two major issues that must be resolved before I can approve anything. First, the lead contamination at 185 ppm requires removal of the top 8 inches of soil and replacement with certified clean soil, with verification testing before any student use. Second, the grant requires 10 native plant species instead of 6, exactly 6 science lessons by November 1, 2026 instead of 3, and supervised maintenance on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 2:30 p.m. Both of these affect the timeline, budget, and operating plan. I'd like both of you to work together to revise the proposal to incorporate the soil remediation, the updated species count, the increased lesson count, the maintenance schedule, and a revised timeline that accounts for remediation before planting. Once I receive the updated plan, I can make my final decision. Are there any other issues either of you is aware of that we haven't yet discussed?
